subject: RayCap connectivity: Private VPC qualification — post-call notes & asks
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@raycap.com>, ops@raycap.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: RayCap Private VPC qualification & next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to meet the team. Summary + asks below to keep momentum. Please reply inline where helpful.

Summary of what we heard (quick):
- Primary preference: private connectivity (PrivateLink preferred) to avoid cross-account peering.
- Security: RayCap requires cert pinning for control channel, per-tenant audit logs, and SOC-2 evidence (we'll follow up with evidence folder).
- Network: RayCap will maintain strict egress allowlist; needs static egress IPs from Redwood and an IP-range for peering if peering chosen.
- Timeline: pilot infra by end of Nov, production by mid-Dec if network is cleared.

Action items for RayCap (please confirm):
1) Confirm PrivateLink vs VPC peering preference (you mentioned PrivateLink orally) — reply with final choice.
2) Share a minimal network diagram (VPCs, subnets, proxy/firewall) + contact for NetOps (name/email).
3) Confirm whether TLS client certs are required from our side for mutual TLS.
4) Provide tentative throughput: concurrent requests / tokens per month and SLOs (p95 latency target).

What we (Redwood) will deliver to you this week:
- VPC connectivity requirements doc (attached: redwood_vpc_requirements.pdf)
- A sample VPC architecture diagram you can adapt (attached)
- High-level dedicated vs hosted decision matrix tailored to your expected throughput

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood_vpc_requirements.pdf (application/pdf)], [Attachment: vpc-architecture-template.png (image/png)]

Next step suggestion: once you confirm PrivateLink and provide NetOps contact, we’ll schedule a 30-min network preflight with our infra eng + your ops to exchange SG/ACL lists and test plan.

Thanks — Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Alice Chen <alice@raycap.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: ops@raycap.com, procurement@raycap.com
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: RayCap Private VPC qualification & next steps

Thanks Evelyn — concise, helpful notes. A few clarifications from our side:

1) PrivateLink preference: confirmed. We cannot do account-to-account peering due to tenancy isolation rules. PrivateLink is the path of least resistance for security/compliance.

2) NetOps contact: Ops lead is Marco Rivera (marco.rivera@raycap.com). He’ll coordinate the diagram and firewall rules.

3) TLS: we require server auth (we validate cert chain). Mutual TLS is preferred but not mandatory for pilot; would like to enable mTLS in prod. Can you send the cert chain/root CA you use for control-plane?

4) Throughput: initial pilot ~200 concurrent small requests (avg 32 tokens per request), estimated monthly tokens ~12M. Latency target p95 < 250ms for short generations. If we scale to Dedicated later, we’ll target higher concurrency.

Procurement note: procurement looped in on SOW; we expect to review draft this week.

On PrivateLink specifics: please confirm the static egress IPs we should allow (or if you provide NAT) and whether we need to open specific ports to a managed endpoint.

Thanks — Alice
Alice Chen
Head of Infrastructure, RayCap Financial Systems

Subject: Re: RayCap connectivity: Private VPC qualification — quick throughput question

Morning — quick follow up from engineering: thanks for the pilot numbers, that helps. One clarifying question before we size pilot vs Dedicated recommendation:

- For the ~200 concurrent small requests, are those parallel synchronous calls (i.e., user-facing real-time) or batched async jobs?

If mostly synchronous (user-facing), our suggested pilot config is a Dedicated small GPU pool (guaranteed concurrency + lower p95), but we can run pilot on Hosted + PrivateLink if you accept potential cold-start variability. If asynchronous/batched, Hosted with higher batching will be more cost-effective.

If you can confirm call type by EOD, we’ll include the concrete pilot sizing and cost delta in the SOW draft for procurement.

Thanks — Aditya
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
